name: security-ingress-annotation-authority-review
intent: Ingress annotations/templates controlling privileged proxy behavior
artifacts: Controller/version, allowed annotations, snippet/template handling, ingress writers and generated proxy config.
trace: Trace an allowed ingress writer field into routing, file access or configuration evaluated by a higher-privilege controller.
experiment: Use an isolated controller fixture and inert routing marker; compare permitted routing and one policy-forbidden annotation effect.
disproof: Controller support for powerful annotations is not tenant escalation unless a lower-trust writer can reach the protected effect.
repair: Constrain annotations/ingress writers and generated configuration, retesting intended routes and rejected privileged directives.
branch_decisions: Identify the installed ingress controller and enabled annotation/template features. The same annotation name can be ignored by a different controller. Separate permission to create Ingress objects from ability to alter global controller configuration; only trace input into generated configuration when a lower-trust actor can set it and the controller actually consumes it.
operational_method: For ingress-nginx, collect the effective controller ConfigMap, snippet enablement, risk admission settings and installed controller version. Retain the generated configuration or rejection diagnostic for the specific annotation. A submitted annotation that is ignored or rejected does not reach the proxy parser. Compare a harmless admitted annotation with the disputed privileged directive in an isolated renderer, and keep permission to edit the controller ConfigMap separate from permission to create an Ingress.
